controls.title: Limit macro use to approved business needs
controls.statement: Disable Microsoft Office macros for users without a business need and permit required macros only from approved trust locations or publishers.
controls.risk: A malicious document could run attacker-controlled commands if users can enable macros that have no approved business purpose.
controls.scope: Microsoft Office users, macro-enabled documents, trusted locations and trusted publishers.
controls.examine: Compare approved macro users and workflows with deployed macro policy, trusted locations, publisher lists and exceptions.
controls.interview: Ask business and application owners how macro need is approved and how trust decisions are reviewed.
controls.test: Use safe signed, unsigned, trusted-location and untrusted test documents with representative users.
test_steps: Choose representative users and Office applications subject to different macro needs and identify approved publishers, locations and business exceptions.
Open safe signed and approved macro documents and verify only the expected users and applications can run the authorised functions.
Open unsigned, Internet-origin, untrusted-location and expired-certificate test documents and confirm macros remain blocked without a simple user override.
Inspect effective policy and event records to confirm the decision, file origin, signature, user and device are visible and exceptions match approval.
controls.expected: Users without an approved need cannot run macros; permitted macros are limited to the configured trusted paths and publishers.

mappings.basis: Requires macros to be disabled for users who do not have a demonstrated business requirement.
Restricts macros to a sandbox, trusted location or trusted publisher in the source scope.
Restricts write access to trusted locations to personnel whose role requires it.
Prevents users from enabling macros signed by an untrusted publisher.
Prevents users from enabling macros that do not use the required version of digital signature.

controls.title: Scan macros and block unsafe capabilities
controls.statement: Scan Office macros for malicious content, block high-risk calls and Internet-sourced macros, and prevent users from weakening the settings.
controls.risk: A permitted or signed macro could still deliver malware if its content and capabilities are not checked and constrained.
controls.scope: Microsoft Office macro scanning, source controls, Win32 API restrictions, signing checks and managed settings.
controls.examine: Inspect macro policies, antivirus integration, Internet-origin controls, Win32 API restrictions, signing validation and annual publisher reviews.
controls.interview: Ask security and application owners how signed macros are checked and how policy failures or malicious detections are handled.
controls.test: Use safe test macros to verify Internet-origin blocking, antivirus scanning, high-risk API blocking and resistance to user policy changes.
test_steps: Prepare safe test macros that exercise antivirus scanning, Internet-origin blocking and representative high-risk behaviours such as process creation or Win32 API use.
Run the samples in an isolated representative environment and confirm each prohibited behaviour is blocked before causing a system change.
Attempt benign variations such as renaming, embedding or moving to a user-writable location to verify controls do not depend only on filename or extension.
Confirm prevention events reach monitoring with file, user, device and rule details, then remove test documents and restore the environment.
controls.expected: Unsafe macros and capabilities are blocked, allowed signed macros are checked as required, and users cannot weaken enforcement.

mappings.basis: Requires macros in files from the Internet to be blocked.
Requires macros to be scanned by antivirus software.
Requires macros to be blocked from making Win32 API calls.
Requires signed or trusted macros to be checked as clean before use.
Requires annual validation of the trusted-publisher list.
Prevents users from changing Microsoft Office macro security settings.
